newsitem.title: USA: Christian Science Church to sell Monitor Radio.
newsitem.headline: Christian Science Church to sell Monitor Radio.

text.p: The Christian Science Church has reached a tentative agreement to sell Monitor Radio, a news network used by more than 200 public radio stations in the United States, network officials said Wednesday.
No price was disclosed for the transaction with World Times, publisher of The WorldPaper, a weekly newspaper.
The deal is contingent on enough stations that broadcast Monitor Radio agreeing to continue airing the programmes under the new ownership, Monitor Radio told the stations.

The Christian Science Church, which also publishes The Christian Science Monitor newspaper, said in April it wanted to sell or discontinue the radio network to concentrate its financial resources on other projects.

"We are pleased to have found an organisation that shares our views on the importance of high quality journalism and that may provide jobs for many of our talented staff members," Monitor editor David Cook said in the statement.

Boston-based World Times has published The WorldPaper since 1979. The weekly is printed in six languages and is distributed on five continents with a 1.5 million circulation but is not available the United States, officials said.
World Times, which has no broadcast operations, is also "in discussions with a prominent public radio organisation regarding collaboration," according to the statement.

Monitor Radio is distributed by Public Radio International, a rival to National Public Radio. Begun in 1984, Monitor Radio is the second-largest provider of news programing to public stations behind NPR and is heard by an estimated 1.1 million people each week.

Stations often use Monitor's programming to supplement NPR's news shows. NPR announced shortly after Monitor Radio was put on the sales block that it would offer a programme in the early morning time slot now occupied by Monitor.
